blocks.answers: Raising the hands at takbir: Sunnah; Nothing: the prayer is valid. Ruku': Pillar; Go back and do it, then sujud as-sahw. Subhana rabbiya l-'azim in ruku': Obligatory; Sujud as-sahw. A surah after al-Fatihah: Sunnah; Nothing: the prayer is valid. Final tashahhud: Pillar; Go back and do it, then sujud as-sahw. Rabbighfir li between the two sujud: Obligatory; Sujud as-sahw. Al-Fatihah: Pillar; Go back and do it, then sujud as-sahw. Right hand over left on the chest: Sunnah; Nothing: the prayer is valid. First tashahhud: Obligatory; Sujud as-sahw. Sujud: Pillar; Go back and do it, then sujud as-sahw. Opening du'a: Sunnah; Nothing: the prayer is valid. Takbir when moving (not the opening): Obligatory; Sujud as-sahw

keywords.def: obligatory acts: if forgotten, made up with sujud as-sahw

questions.q: Explain the difference between a pillar and an obligatory act.
questions.a: A pillar cannot be replaced: it must be done; an obligatory act forgotten is made up by sujud as-sahw.

questions.q: Raising the hands at takbir is ...
Classify twelve acts on the pupil PDF as pillar, obligatory or sunnah, and write what to do if each is forgotten.
questions.a: Classified correctly following the lesson table, with the repair for each

questions.q: Extend: what is said between the two sujud?
Stretch: why might the four schools classify some acts differently?
questions.a: They weighed the evidence and wording of hadith differently; all aim to follow the Sunnah.

questions.q: Bilal forgets the first tashahhud. What should he do?
options: Complete the prayer and do sujud as-sahw
questions.a: A) Complete the prayer and do sujud as-sahw. The first tashahhud is obligatory; forgetting it is made up with sujud as-sahw (Bukhari and Muslim).

questions.q: Forgetting an obligatory act is repaired by ...
Think again: must you always start again?
questions.a: No: sujud as-sahw repairs a forgotten obligatory act.
